title: INC-104 · Hostel Uplink Imbalance
summary: Two monitored paths report a fixed 100 Mbps total, but a second sensor only repeats the first measurement.
description: During the evening peak the gateway reported 100 Mbps split across two hostel uplinks. An operator noted that one link was 100 Mbps more than zero, but the second sensor repeated the same relationship in doubled form. The model has fewer independent constraints than unknowns.
investigationSteps: Identify unknowns from the affected links.
Translate each sensor reading into one linear equation.
Reduce the augmented matrix and inspect the rank.
Decide whether the split is uniquely identifiable.
templateFindings: The second equation is exactly twice the first, so it adds no independent information.
The coefficient matrix has rank 1 for 2 unknowns, which means infinitely many valid traffic splits.
One additional independent measurement is required to identify a unique distribution.
suggestedActions: Add a sensor that measures the difference between the two uplinks.
Re-run the model once a truly independent equation is available.
Do not report a specific per-link value until the system is fully determined.
